title: Posture and wrist health for needlework
subtitle: How to set up your working position to avoid strain during long sessions.
excerpt: Embroidery sessions of more than an hour put repeated strain on the wrists, neck, and upper back. Small adjustments to how you sit, hold the hoop, and take breaks make a significant difference. This reading covers the main habits that prevent common overuse problems.
sourceNotes: Ergonomics guidance synthesised from contemporary needlework practice and general repetitive-strain literature.

glossaryTerms.definition: Injury or discomfort from repeating a small movement over a long period without adequate rest. In needlework, the wrist, thumb, forefinger, and neck are the most commonly affected areas.

content.text: from needlework usually develops slowly. Sessions feel fine until one day the wrist aches after ten minutes. The habits in this reading are easier to build before that point than after.

Sit with the work at elbow height. If the hoop is too low you will hunch forward; if it is too high your shoulders will creep up. Both positions fatigue the upper back within 20 to 30 minutes. A lap stand or floor stand that holds the hoop frees both hands and keeps the work at the right height.

Hold the hoop loosely. A tight grip fatigues the hand quickly. The hoop should rest against the heel of the palm and the fingers should guide it, not grip it. Change the position of the hoop in your hand every few minutes when working in the same area for a long stretch.

Keep the stitching wrist in a neutral position: neither bent up nor bent down. A bent wrist while pulling thread narrows the carpal tunnel and increases strain. If you find yourself bending the wrist to pull thread through, adjust the angle at which you hold the hoop instead.

Take a one-minute break every 20 to 30 minutes. Set the hoop down, open and close the hand a few times, and roll the wrists in circles. This is not wasted time. It extends the length of a comfortable session considerably. Most professional embroiderers work in short focused blocks rather than unbroken hours.
